question: A film app shows an average of 3.9 stars from users. Who mostly wrote those ratings?
options: Viewers who loved or hated it
answer: Viewers who loved or hated it. Hu, Pavlou and Zhang found online ratings pile up at five stars with a smaller spike at one, a J shape, because people who felt strongly are the ones who bother to write. The lukewarm majority stays silent, so the average describes the motivated few.
move: Ask who bothered to answer before trusting what the answers say.
ask: Before I trust the next star rating I see, who probably bothered to leave it?
trap: A fair cross-section of viewers, since anyone could rate it.
reference: Hu, Pavlou and Zhang, Overcoming the J-shaped Distribution of Product Reviews, Communications of the ACM, 52(10), 2009
